prompt.context: You have been hired by the internal strategy group at Yahoo. You are asked to analyze the recent acquisition of YouTube, an online video community, by Google for $1.6 billion.
prompt.question: Is this acquisition a competitive threat for Yahoo?

clarifying_info.q: What is YouTube's current user base?
Should we account for user base growth or attrition?
clarifying_info.a: Assume no user base growth or attrition

clarifying_info.q: What discount rate should we use?
What is Google's pricing and margin assumption for YouTube?
clarifying_info.a: Google believes it can charge $150 per user annually and make 67% margins

framework: Assess each company's core competencies and strategic positioning
Evaluate the strategic rationale behind the Google-YouTube acquisition
Determine whether the acquisition constitutes a competitive threat to Yahoo
Develop a competitive response for Yahoo
Quantify whether Google can break even on the acquisition given stated assumptions

questions.prompt: Part I: Is Google's acquisition of YouTube a competitive threat to Yahoo? Analyze the strategic positioning of both Yahoo and Google.
questions.guidance: Yahoo is a destination site focused on keeping users engaged within its ecosystem to drive ad clicks and e-commerce/subscription revenue; it monetizes time and wallet. Google is primarily a search engine that has built ad-targeting technology around search intent — it has consumer eyeballs but not wallet share. YouTube represents Google's move toward community-building and user engagement, directly overlapping with Yahoo's strategy. The acquisition is therefore a competitive threat because it helps Google monetize traffic through community, not just search.

questions.prompt: Part II: Yahoo wants to counter this threat. Assume feasibility and cost are not a concern. Develop a competitive response for Yahoo.
questions.guidance: Candidate should take a moment to structure ideas before speaking. Strong answers demonstrate creativity and business judgment. Suggested directions: (1) Create a Yahoo-branded video community offering to directly counter YouTube; (2) Acquire Google itself; (3) Enable real-time video sharing among friends from mobile devices via a cross-selling partnership; (4) Build or crowdsource creative video backdrops from historical events, sporting arenas, or famous films — letting users re-enact scenes or create collaborative videos (e.g., a rock stadium backdrop where friends can jam and make a music video).

questions.prompt: Part III: Google proceeds with the acquisition and believes it can charge $150 per user annually at 67% margins. Can Google break even with its current user base?
questions.guidance: Calculate annual margin per user, then total annual margin, and compare to the $1.6B acquisition cost. The answer is yes — Google will break even in under two years at current user base with these assumptions.

math.setup: Acquisition cost = $1.6B. User base = 40M. Revenue per user = $150/year. Margin rate = 67%. Margin per user = $150 × 67% = $100/year. Break-even margin per user needed = $1,600M / 40M = $40. Since actual margin per user ($100) exceeds the required break-even margin per user ($40), Google will break even.
steps: Required margin per user to recover acquisition cost = $1,600M ÷ 40M users = $40/user
$100 actual > $40 required → Google breaks even (in approximately 1.6 billion / (40M × $100) = 0.4 years, i.e., about 5 months)
math.answer: Yes, Google can break even. Actual margin per user ($100/year) exceeds the required break-even margin per user ($40), so Google recovers the $1.6B acquisition cost well within one year at current user base.

brainstorming.prompt: What creative responses could Yahoo pursue to counter the Google-YouTube threat?

categories.name: Build (organic)
ideas: Launch a Yahoo-branded video community platform
Develop mobile real-time video sharing features
Open-source or crowdsource creative video backdrops and scene re-enactment tools

categories.name: Buy (M&A)
ideas: Acquire another video or social media platform to compete directly

categories.name: Partner (alliance)
ideas: Partner with mobile device makers to enable real-time video sharing from phones or wearables
Cross-sell video creation tools with hardware/device partners

recommendation: Yes, Google's acquisition of YouTube is a competitive threat to Yahoo because it moves Google toward community-building and user engagement — Yahoo's core strategic territory
Yahoo should respond by developing or acquiring a competing video community, and by leveraging its existing user base and destination-site positioning to differentiate
risks: Google's brand strength in search may allow rapid YouTube monetization, accelerating competitive pressure
Yahoo may lack the technical talent or platform infrastructure to build a competitive video product quickly
Any M&A response by Yahoo carries integration and execution risk
next_steps: Conduct a detailed build-vs-buy analysis for a Yahoo video community product
Assess partnership opportunities with mobile/device players for real-time video sharing
Monitor YouTube user growth and monetization rate to track competitive threat over time
